commits.subject: fix(diagram): harden fragments and make rendering byte-stable
commits.body:
Address an independent review of the diagram renderer:

- Give every fragment attribute a value grammar instead of rejecting
  url( and javascript: substrings; CSS escapes could otherwise smuggle an
  external reference into a published slide.
- Refuse repeated attributes, which produced SVG that does not parse,
  and mixed text content, which was silently reordered.
- Cap fragment nesting and total fragment bytes so a small source cannot
  render hundreds of megabytes.
- Write text elements inline: indentation inside xml:space=preserve text
  shifted middle- and end-aligned labels.
- Round coordinates to thousandths and prevent fused multiply-add, so
  arm64 and amd64 render identical bytes and diagram check agrees across
  machines.
- Validate styles in sorted order, refuse case-variant update keys,
  edges with both a path and points, and icons on non-nodes, and always
  store an elements array.

commits.subject: Add inventory format 2 record types and read compatibility
commits.body:
Introduce the canonical persisted contract for proposed/implemented technical
inventory without adding any writer: evidence references with stable IDs
unique per revision, explicit revision intent with an implemented baseline or
explicit none, delivery {repository, commit}, data entities (curated fields,
holding Component pins, owned association/production relationships), authored
ERD roots with offline SVG visuals, directory and bindings, and ERD overlays
with pins and proposed removals. Items gain documentation_view and explicit
selections.

Format 2 is opt-in: ___inventory/format.json must exist before any new kind or
intent is read, and older readers refuse the marker, the new directories and
the new Item fields rather than silently dropping them. Legacy revisions are
unchanged and read as unspecified intent. Loading validates each record
structurally (baseline must be an implemented ancestor, unsafe or external SVG
content is refused); cross-record policy checks belong to the writers.

ResolveSelection gives consumers one structural path/evidence resolver with
stable reason codes, and ComposeOverlay applies an overlay to its baseline ERD
directory without modifying the canonical record. Query and server call sites
only adapt to the Evidence type.

commits.subject: Remember content-addressed Git answers across commands
commits.body:
Merge-bases, ancestry, first parents, and diffs of full commit IDs can
never change while those commits exist, so a process-wide cache keeps
them across commands and server requests. Existence is the one thing
that can change: gc prunes unreachable commits, as after a squash merge.
A remembered answer is served only after the session's cat-file process
confirms every commit it names is still present, and existence checks
and object reads are never cached. Cached diffs also key on the
checkout's top-level attribute files, which Git reads even between
commits.

commits.subject: Remember ref- and config-dependent Git answers until they can change
commits.body:

remembered across commands and server requests. Each answer is served
only while its repository's state digest is unchanged: the contents of
HEAD, every loose ref, packed-refs, the reftable table list, the
repository and global configuration, and the Git environment. Git
rewrites all of these through lock files, so detection does not depend
on timestamp resolution. A root is re-asked when a .git appears between
the directory and its top level. Full and abbreviated object IDs, reflog
selectors, and paths are never remembered this way. Tests cover commits,
checkouts, resets, packed refs, branch deletion, linked worktrees,
set-url, a global insteadOf rule, and repositories appearing and
disappearing around a directory.

commits.author: trevor@twentyideas.com <trevor@twentyideas.com>
commits.subject: Close the configuration gap and isolate only diffs in the server
commits.body:
Isolating every cached answer from server requests cost the server
suite 2,800 Git processes. Only one input is truly out of reach: the
attributes Git reads from the checkout when diffing, nested
.gitattributes included. So:

- Configuration answers now count every file Git reads: the repository's,
  the system and global files git var reports, and every file those
  include, followed recursively whatever the include's condition. A path
  the parser cannot resolve exactly (escapes, %(prefix)) disables
  remembering rather than guessing, as does a Git that cannot report its
  configuration files.
- A remembered repository root also checks that digest, since
  core.worktree, core.bare, and safe.directory can move or refuse it.
- Merge-bases, ancestry, and first parents depend on commits alone and
  are remembered in every process, still only while the commits exist.
- Diffs are the one answer a long-running process remembers per session:
  StableDiff keeps them for the request that read them.

Tests edit nested and relative includes, the system file, and
core.worktree between commands and check the next one sees the change.

commits.author: trevor@twentyideas.com <trevor@twentyideas.com>
commits.subject: Find repositories from standard output and remember them race-free
commits.body:
Review findings:
- rev-parse ran through CombinedOutput, so GIT_TRACE or any warning on
  standard error broke finding the repository. It now reads standard
  output and takes Git's message from standard error on failure.
- A relative --git-common-dir was joined onto a path that could still
  contain symlinks, placing the git directory somewhere that does not
  exist; the digest then hashed missing files and never saw HEAD move.
  --path-format=absolute resolves both directories physically, and a
  digest refuses git directories that do not exist.
- Configuration was digested after Git answered, so a change in between
  was remembered as the answer for the new configuration. The git
  directories are now found without Git first, their configuration is
  digested before Git answers and again after, and the answer is kept
  only when Git agrees with the guess and nothing changed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: trevor@twentyideas.com <trevor@twentyideas.com>
commits.subject: File remembered ref answers only under digests read around the answer
commits.body:
Review finding: an answer was stored under the digest taken before
Git answered, and within a session under the session's digest, which can
be much older (a background build). If the repository moved and then
returned to that state, the answer described the state in between. It
is now stored only when digests read fresh immediately before and after
the answer agree.

Regression tests: a checkout during an answer, and a symlinked checkout
whose remote URL and packed refs change (the misplaced common directory
hid both).

so a comparison's file order depended on whether a session batched its
diffs. -O/dev/null makes both ignore it, like every other user setting
the canonical diff overrides.

commits.subject: Never remember revisions rooted in a pseudo-ref

in the git directory that the state digest does not cover, so a fetch
or merge could move one unseen: serve --against FETCH_HEAD kept the old
base after git fetch. Revisions rooted in them are now always asked.

commits.author: trevor@twentyideas.com <trevor@twentyideas.com>
commits.subject: Account for rewritten history and branch-conditional configuration
commits.body:

- Grafts, a shallow boundary, and replace refs change what Git reports
  for the same commit IDs, so remembered merge-bases, ancestry, and first
  parents could outlive one. A repository with any of them is now never
  remembered this way; the check runs once per session.
- [includeIf "onbranch:..."] makes configuration follow HEAD, which the
  configuration digest did not cover, so a checkout alone could leave a
  stale remote URL. HEAD is now part of it.

- A caller waiting for a busy batch pool ignored its context. acquire

commits.subject: Support Git before 2.31 and keep memoized answers out of the caches
commits.body:
Review round two:
- A: --path-format=absolute needs Git 2.31, and older Git echoes an
  unknown flag to standard output, so repository discovery failed on
  every command with Git 2.25 to 2.30. Discovery now asks only
  rev-parse --show-toplevel --git-dir --git-common-dir and resolves

- C: revisions through main-worktree/ and worktrees/ read HEAD files the

commits.subject: Flag proposals that take in new lines, show neighbouring hunks, and refuse brace-only anchors
commits.body:
A proposal is widened whenever it takes in lines the pinned range did not
have, not only when a hunk crosses its edge, so a sibling function git slid
inside the range is flagged. Its diff shows the nearest hunk just before and
after the range, so an extracted helper or move is visible. Nothing is
proposed when the only lines an edit left in the range are braces, blank, or
punctuation, which anchor nothing.
